item.title: Excel 3 — Sat Nov 7, 10:30 AM — Montclair Main - Conference Room
item.description:
The class is geared to beginners and those who seek a refresher in the topic. Students will gain a basic understanding of the worksheet environment, tools for working with data, and resources for continued learning.
This is a hands-on class; students should be able to use the mouse and keyboard. Students are welcome to bring a flash drive to save their work for review and practice.
Summary of Topics:
Class 1: Worksheet basics using a budget - Learn elements of the worksheet, enter and edit budget data, perform calculations, create a pie chart.
Class 2: Format a worksheet for an attractive, easily-readable on-screen presentation as well with the attributes needed for printing.
Class 3: Formulas & Functions – learn more about how to use formulas, and the wide array of built-in functions. item.title: "The Ride" - Music and Storytelling from the American West — Sat Nov 7, 2:00 PM — Montclair Main - Auditorium
item.description:
Inspired by his lifelong love affair with the American West, Marc Berger, a nationally touring artist, performs songs from his album, "Ride." Join us for an evening showcase of ten cinematic songs capturing the vastness and romance of the West while exploring its deep roots in the American psyche.
From the haunting message and beat of “Twister” and the soul-shaking challenge of taming a wild horse in “Take it on the Chin”, to the sexy, mind-blowing, middle-of-nowhere encounter of “Time Waits For No Man” and on through seven more scenic stops, RIDE takes you on a dusty tour of the Great American Frontier
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Memory Café - A Dementia-Friendly Social Gathering — Mon Nov 9, 11:30 AM — Montclair Main - Cafe Area
item.description:
For adults with dementia and their caregivers, this event offers a welcoming, safe, calming space for socializing, music, art and reminiscing every month.
A “Memory Café” is a dementia-friendly social gathering for individuals with early-stage memory loss or mild cognitive decline and their care givers.
The meetings will be held in a safe and comfortable environment where people can interact and socialize with others having similar experiences. At the gatherings participants can get support in a non-judgmental setting, while enjoying the benefits of music for the brain.
The meetings will be run by Lisy Espindola, LCSW and Kim McLennon, MSW and music therapist. Lunch and/or snacks will be served.
This is a joint program between Lifelong Montclair at the Township of Montclair and the Montclair Public Library.
Attendance is free but registration is required. Questions? Call 973-744-3278.

item.title: Your Library, Your Voice: Help Shape the New Library! — Mon Nov 16, 12:30 PM — Montclair Main - Tower Room
item.description:
What does the library mean to you? As we prepare for our upcoming renovation, we want to build a space that truly serves our community—and that starts with listening to you.
Join us for an open feedback session to share whatever is on your mind:
How you use the library today
What you love about our programs, collections, and spaces
Frustrations or obstacles you've run into
What you’d love to see in the renovated space
Whether you have big design ideas or just want to tell us about your favorite books, we're all ears. Your feedback will directly guide the design, programs, and future of our library.
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

Please sign up for a 30-minute consultation with our Youth Services Reading Specialist. Some topics may include:
How to support your child's reading at home Review your child's current reading assessment (please bring copies, if possible) Learn what resources we have at the library to check out for your developing or struggling reader Other areas of concern or curiosity regarding your child's literacy development
Sign up HERE for a slot!
Adults only. Registration is required.

item.title: Tech Talks: Fact-Checking & Misinformation — Tue Nov 17, 3:30 PM — Montclair Main - Classroom
item.description:
Tech Talks is a free informational series where library staff introduce and explain the technology topics that matter most in today's digital world. Each session takes a closer look at a new or complex topic—whether it's a trending app, an emerging technology, or a platform you've been hearing about but aren't quite sure how to navigate. Through demonstrations and clear, jargon-free explanations, you'll come away with a better understanding of the tech landscape around you. There's no hands-on component, so no devices are needed—just come ready to learn and ask questions.
All are welcome regardless of experience level, and time is reserved at the end of each session for Q&A. Sessions are free and open to the public.
This week's topic is: Fact-Checking & Misinformation

item.title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day — Sun Dec 6, 9:00 AM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group **TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are almost finished!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site.
Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). Tools, water, and a snack will be provided. (Registration is not required though if you sign up on Meetup, it helps us know how many tools to bring.) Only heavy, steady rain cancels.
Source: Meetup: South Mountain Conservancy
